learn.hook: Two friends both made 5,072 on a button calculator — one used 14 clicks, the other used 77! Who was smarter?
points: A number can be built in many ways: 5,072 = 5 thousands + 7 tens + 2 ones = 50 hundreds + 72 ones.
Fewest clicks: use the biggest buttons first. The fewest clicks equal the sum of the digits: 5,072 needs 5 + 0 + 7 + 2 = 14.
Why? Ten clicks of a button can always be replaced by one click of the next bigger button, so no button needs more than 9 clicks.
The fewest-click way is the expanded form: 5,072 = 5 × 1000 + 0 × 100 + 7 × 10 + 2 × 1.
With a fixed number of clicks, the largest number puts all clicks on the biggest button; the smallest 5-digit number with 5 clicks is 10,004.

quiz.q: How many whole numbers round to 70 when rounded to the nearest ten?

quiz.q: How many whole numbers round to 3,000 when rounded to the nearest hundred?

quiz.q: Which number rounds to 8,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?

quiz.mistake: Thinks 8,500 rounds down

quiz.q: In which situation should you round UP?

Finding how many full boxes you can fill
Writing the exact amount on a cheque
Reading the price on a bill

Packing all 130 mangoes: the leftover mangoes still need a box.
'How many full boxes' rounds down; a cheque and a bill must be exact.
So round up when finding boxes needed to pack all 130 mangoes.
Answer: Finding how many boxes are needed to pack all 130 mangoes
quiz.mistake: Does not think about what happens to the leftover

quiz.q: Between which two neighbouring hundreds does 6,47,382 lie?

quiz.mistake: Gives the neighbouring thousands or tens instead

topics.title: How close is an estimate? Census tables

learn.hook: An estimate is a guess with a fence around it — we can say exactly how far off it could be!
points: If each number is rounded to the nearest thousand, each can be off by up to 500, so a sum of two can be off by up to 1,000.
Rounding both numbers down gives a lower bound; rounding both up gives an upper bound. The exact sum lies between them.
In a census table, subtract the earlier population from the later one to find the increase.
'Nearly doubled' means the new value is about 2 times the old. Divide to see how many times bigger.
Compare increases, not just populations, to see which place grew the most.

example.q: Sonpur had 4,20,000 people in 2001 and 8,30,000 in 2021. Did it nearly double?

learn.reallife: Every 10 years India's census counts its people; planners use these tables to decide how many schools and hospitals a town needs.

games.title: Bounds and growth
items: For 3,280 + 4,610, the sum 3,000 + 4,000 = 7,000 is a lower bound
Both were rounded down, and the exact sum is 7,890.
For 3,280 + 4,610, the sum 4,000 + 5,000 = 9,000 is an upper bound
Both were rounded up.
The exact sum can be less than the lower bound
Rounding both down can only make the sum smaller, never bigger.
A town growing from 5 lakh to 9.8 lakh has nearly doubled
2 × 5 lakh = 10 lakh, and 9.8 lakh is close.
Growing from 2 lakh to 3 lakh is a bigger increase than from 10 lakh to 10.5 lakh
1 lakh is more than 50,000.

quiz.q: Sonpur's population (made-up data) was 4,20,000 in 2001 and 6,10,000 in 2011. By how much did it grow?
quiz.explain: Increase = later − earlier = 6,10,000 − 4,20,000 = 1,90,000.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two populations

quiz.q: Sonpur grew from 4,20,000 (2001) to 6,10,000 (2011) to 8,30,000 (2021). In which decade did it grow more?
quiz.explain: 2001–2011: 1,90,000. 2011–2021: 2,20,000. The second decade had the bigger increase.
quiz.mistake: Compares the populations instead of the increases

quiz.q: Rampur grew from 1,50,000 to 2,95,000 in ten years. Which describes this best?
quiz.explain: Double of 1,50,000 is 3,00,000, and 2,95,000 is very close to that.
quiz.mistake: Confuses doubling with tripling

quiz.q: In 2021, Sonpur had 8,30,000 people and Rampur had 4,15,000. How many times Rampur's population is Sonpur's?
steps: So Sonpur's population is 2 times Rampur's.

quiz.q: Without adding exactly, which range must contain 38,760 + 51,430?
quiz.explain: Round both down: 38,000 + 51,000 = 89,000. Round both up: 39,000 + 52,000 = 91,000. The exact sum (90,190) is in between.
quiz.mistake: Rounds one number up and the other down and calls it a bound

quiz.q: Two numbers are each rounded to the nearest thousand and then added. At most, how far can this estimate be from the exact sum?
quiz.explain: Each rounding can be off by up to 500, and two such errors can add up to 1,000.
quiz.mistake: Counts the error of only one number

quiz.q: Estimate 7,48,000 − 2,61,000 by rounding each to the nearest lakh. How far is the estimate from the exact difference?
quiz.mistake: Gives the estimate instead of the gap

quiz.q: From 2011 to 2021, which town had the largest increase: Sonpur (6,10,000 → 8,30,000), Rampur (2,95,000 → 4,15,000) or Devgarh (5,00,000 → 6,50,000)?
quiz.explain: Increases: Sonpur 2,20,000, Rampur 1,20,000, Devgarh 1,50,000. Sonpur grew the most.

topics.title: How long is the product? Patterns and enough information

points: A 3-digit number × a 2-digit number has 4 or 5 digits: 100 × 10 = 1,000 is the smallest and 999 × 99 = 98,901 is the largest.
In general, an a-digit number × a b-digit number has (a + b − 1) or (a + b) digits.
Before solving, check if the information is enough. 'How many people live in the building?' needs the flats AND the people in each flat.

learn.hook: Write 1, 2, 3, ... side by side: 123456789101112... What is the 1000th digit? Let's find out!
points: Using each digit 0–9 once, the largest number is 9,876,543,210. It ends in 0, so it is also the largest multiple of 5.
The smallest even 10-digit number using each digit once is 1,023,456,798 — it must end in an even digit.
To strike out digits and leave the largest number, keep the biggest digits as far left as possible.
If the digits are in increasing order (like 123456789), swapping any two of them makes the number larger.
Counting digits: 1–9 use 9 digits, 10–99 use 180 digits, and each number from 100 to 999 uses 3.

steps: 1 to 9 use 9 digits; 10 to 99 use 180 more: total 189
811 = 3 × 270 + 1, so 270 three-digit numbers (100 to 369) are used fully
The next digit is the first digit of 370

games.title: Puzzle facts
items: Every multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5

It ends in 9, which is odd.
To get the largest number after striking digits, keep big digits on the left

quiz.q: What is the largest multiple of 5 that uses each digit 0–9 exactly once?
quiz.explain: It must end in 0 or 5. Ending in 0 lets 9, 8, 7, ... stay in front: 9876543210.
steps: Put 0 last and the rest in decreasing order
quiz.mistake: Forgets to use each digit exactly once, or forgets the 0-or-5 rule

quiz.q: What is the smallest even 10-digit number that uses each digit 0–9 exactly once?
quiz.explain: Start 1, 0, 2, 3, ... to keep it small. 1023456789 ends in 9 (odd), so swap the last two: 1023456798.
steps: Remaining 8 and 9: end with 8 to be even
quiz.mistake: Ignores that the number must be even

quiz.q: Strike out 3 digits from 4719283 so that the number left is as large as possible.
quiz.explain: Choose 9 first (it is among the first four digits). After 9 only 2, 8, 3 remain and we need all of them: 9283.
steps: Pick the biggest possible first digit: 9
quiz.mistake: Rearranges the digits instead of only striking some

quiz.q: Which 9-digit number, using digits 1–9 once, becomes larger whenever you swap any two of its digits?
quiz.explain: In 123456789 every digit is smaller than all digits to its right, so any swap moves a bigger digit to the left.
steps: Swapping puts the larger digit in the higher place
So digits must be in increasing order
quiz.mistake: Picks the largest arrangement instead of the smallest

quiz.q: If we write 1, 2, 3, 4, ... side by side, what is the 1000th digit?
quiz.explain: 189 digits are used up to 99. 811 more digits = 270 three-digit numbers (up to 369) plus 1 digit. That digit is the 3 of 370.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that numbers from 10 to 99 have 2 digits each

quiz.q: How many digits are used to write all the numbers from 1 to 99 side by side?
quiz.explain: 1 to 9: 9 digits. 10 to 99: 90 numbers × 2 digits = 180. Total 189.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the single-digit numbers

quiz.q: Ignoring spaces and hyphens, which number name has the most letters?
quiz.explain: seventy-seven has 7 + 5 = 12 letters; one hundred has 10; forty-four has 9; sixty-six has 8.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger number always has a longer name

quiz.q: Which number has the longest name in words?
quiz.explain: 7,77,777 is 'seven lakh seventy-seven thousand seven hundred seventy-seven' — far longer than 'ten lakh', 'nine lakh' or 'one crore'.
steps: 10,00,000 = ten lakh; 9,00,000 = nine lakh; 1,00,00,000 = one crore.
7,77,777 = seven lakh seventy-seven thousand seven hundred seventy-seven.
Many non-zero digits make a long name, so 7,77,777 has the longest name.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger number always has a longer name
